cross_references.note: CLRA + UCL is the standard California consumer fraud package. CLRA violation = UCL unlawful prong. CLRA provides actual damages + §3294 punitive damages; UCL provides restitution + injunction. The claims are always pled together. CLRA's 30-day cure demand is UCL's companion — send CLRA demand first, then UCL injunction if not cured.

Rees-Levering §2981.9 violation = UCL unlawful prong (borrowing the statutory violation). UCL restitution = all payments made on void contracts. UCL injunction = prohibition on dealer's continued use of non-compliant contract forms.

Rosenthal Act violation = UCL unlawful prong (borrowing Rosenthal violation). FDCPA violation also borrows into UCL unlawful prong. UCL claim against collector adds restitution of all amounts collected through illegal means.

Federal FCRA violation = UCL unlawful prong (Cel-Tech: borrowed violation from federal law). California plaintiffs can assert FCRA violations in California state court via UCL unlawful prong even if FCRA's own standing requirements are not met (avoids Spokeo/TransUnion federal standing gate).

UCL does not provide attorney fees directly. CCP §1021.5 private attorney general fees are available when a UCL case vindicates a significant public right. For individual consumer fraud cases, fees typically run through the companion CLRA (mandatory fees), Rees-Levering §2983.4 (mandatory fees), or Rosenthal §1788.30(c) (mandatory fees).
